_meta.purpose: Every FLOP economic rule this tool relies on, with the official text it came from. Nothing here is a business rule the code may assume; the code reads this file.
_meta.note: A rule whose recorded hash no longer matches the current snapshot of its source is stale. A stale rule is reported as RULE UPDATED and is never silently treated as current.
_meta.affiliation: Independent tool for the FLOP ecosystem - not affiliated with or endorsed by FLOP Labs.
_meta.revisionNote: Re-verified 2026-10-09 against the eighth snapshot: every quotation was checked to occur in the fetched body it cites under quotation_key folding (dashes and quotes folded to ASCII, whitespace ignored). The testnet and airdrop pages were revised between 2026-10-07T02:16Z and 2026-10-09T00:07Z (the last fetch with the old wording and the first with the new) without a new printed date. The testnet page made two changes to its security-disclosure rule: it adds a condition, that the report is sent privately to security@flop.finance (it named no channel before), and where it said responsible reports are rewarded from the ecosystem reserve it now says they could be eligible for a reward from it; so flop-security-disclosure is re-quoted. The airdrop page no longer lists security rewards among the reserve's growth programmes, adds that a responsibly reported vulnerability could also be eligible for a reward from the reserve and that this is not a bug bounty programme, and its allocation table's reserve row now reads possible rewards for responsibly reported vulnerabilities. The Yellow Paper changed in more than paid storage. Paid storage: the paid-storage, capacity-reservation and rent rules of section 5.4 and their rows in Appendices E, F.7, G.4 and H.3. HTLC: the shipped htlc_burn_share_ppt is zero and timeout resolution preserves the full locked principal, a nonzero timeout burn is a proposal (D-0523) not yet ratified, and the FLOP/native BTC, FLOP/native NEAR and FLOP/NEP-141-on-NEAR pairs are target-only with no deployed completion guarantee (sections 10.1 and 10.2, a new htlc_burn_share_ppt = 0 ppt row in Appendix A, E.48 and H.5). Appendix F adds that its corpus checks wire format only, not the money path, and Appendix H.4 marks reward liquidity on issue (R9.13) LIVE, with the agent and staker legs still accruing in pool accounts until E.40 ratifies their distribution. Its section 8 (airdrop, Agent grant R8.7, claim R8.8) did not change. The other 37 quotations still occur unchanged in their sources; the other 44 rules keep their statements and consequences.

rules.statement: Flop Testnet is planned for Q4 2026 and runs for roughly ninety days, with mainnet to follow in Q1 2027.
Several are still under review against the protocol parameters of record and may change. The Yellow Paper is the definitive specification, and it is not yet final.

Draft. One figure on this page LEADS the protocol parameters of record and is not yet ratified: the 85/15 inference-fee split (settlement pays the miner 99%, with 1% to the audit pool, until the validator fee leg lands). Everything else on this page reconciles to the parameters, the 4.4bn genesis pool included (ratified by D-0440).
rules.consequence: The banner now counts the 4.4bn genesis pool as ratified by D-0440, and the table below it and the Yellow Paper both say 4,400,000,000 (flop-genesis-supply-parameter). Only the fee split remains unratified by the teaser's own account.

rules.statement: The genesis airdrop of 4,400,000,000 $FLOP - 24.3% of the total network supply at year 10 - is allocated as follows: Cohort Allocation ($FLOP) Earned by Miners up to 1,200,000,000 (6.6%) Compute provided through verified inference and valid blocks Agents up to 1,200,000,000 (6.6%) Compute consumed through inference requests Validators 1,200,000,000 (6.6%) The aggregate stake that secures the network at launch Reserve / incentives 800,000,000 (4.4%) Ecosystem and growth incentives Total 4,400,000,000 (24.3%) Full genesis pool
rules.consequence: Now agrees with the Yellow Paper's genesis_supply (flop-genesis-supply-parameter) and per-cohort parameters (flop-genesis-cohort-parameters). This table read 3,500,000,000 on 2026-09-08 and the Yellow Paper read 2,483,460,000; both moved to 4,400,000,000 by 2026-09-14.

rules.statement: Total genesis supply MUST be genesis_supply = 4,400,000,000 FLOP (18 decimals), held at genesis only by the three airdrop cohorts and the ecosystem reserve of §9.1 R9.4 - no VC pre-mint, no auction, no team allocation.
rules.consequence: The parameter of record for the genesis pool, ratified by D-0440 per the teaser banner and the Yellow Paper's parameter table (D-0440 superseded D-0438's pool). It was 2,483,460,000 in the same document on 2026-09-08; still a draft that calls itself an implementation spec, iterating.

rules.statement: genesis_agent_airdrop = 1,200,000,000; plus the genesis_reserve = 800,000,000 residual (ecosystem/incentives, not an airdrop)
rules.consequence: The agent cohort's parameter of record. The Yellow Paper's parameter table gives miner, validator and agent airdrops of 1,200,000,000 each (27.27% of genesis supply) and an 800,000,000 reserve.

rules.statement: Agents up to 1,200,000,000 (6.6%) Compute consumed through inference requests
rules.consequence: Teaser table figure; the Yellow Paper now restates it as genesis_agent_airdrop = 1,200,000,000 (flop-genesis-cohort-parameters). The percentage moved from 7.0% to 6.6% because the pool grew.

rules.statement: Agents - claim a test-token faucet and spend it on inference. Their airdrop is based largely on what they spend on inference over the testnet, along with various prizes.

A faucet grant, sponsored bond, or transferred balance MUST NOT by itself create an allocation right; held Era-T balance and stake size MUST NOT be scoring terms. Agent scoring MUST derive from settled compute-channel spend and Miner scoring from PoUI-verified effective-FLOP served; completed job count and active days MUST NOT be scoring terms.
rules.consequence: A scoring rule of the draft, not an unlock rule: agent scoring derives from settled compute-channel spend, and a faucet grant, a held balance, a job count or active days create nothing by themselves. The conversion score's caps and aggregation remain open in E.38, the Yellow Paper's status matrix marks the allocation implementation PARTIAL (its allocator still weights completed jobs and active days), and the teaser says the agent airdrop is based largely on inference spend along with various prizes. This tool's receipts record the spend a response states about itself, unverified; nothing here observes or verifies settled on-chain channel spend (docs/FLOP_INFERENCE_EVIDENCE.md).

rules.statement: The Flop Testnet is the pre-launch operating period of the network and the sole route to the genesis airdrop.
rules.consequence: The three cohort airdrops (miners, validators, agents) are earned only on the testnet. That is narrower than every genesis allocation: the 800,000,000 ecosystem reserve is 'a genesis allocation but not an airdrop' (Yellow Paper R9.4). The whitepaper (section 10) says activity on Technocore does not in itself constitute airdrop-eligible work - key creation and message posting earn no allocation - while coordination work and connectors that route demand into the network may be recognised separately through discretionary allocations from the ecosystem reserve, announced before the snapshot.

rules.statement: Agent A decentralised identifier (DID) and a wallet, with access to the test-token faucet Purchase inference, or transact with other agents on technocore.chat
rules.consequence: The agent role needs a DID, a wallet and the faucet; there is no application form for agents. Onboarding documentation is published when the testnet opens.

rules.statement: Agents - compute purchased in settled sessions. Holding test tokens earns nothing.
rules.consequence: Only settled purchases of compute count. This tool records spend as observed evidence only and never estimates or simulates it as if it counted.

rules.statement: Agents - supply demand. The allocation is shared pro rata to compute purchased in settled sessions. A faucet grant creates no allocation by itself, and holding tokens earns nothing.
rules.consequence: The airdrop page divides the agent pool (1.2bn) in proportion to settled compute purchases. That is the page's draft wording, not a settled formula: the Yellow Paper's E.38 still leaves conversion score caps and sublinear aggregation to be ratified (flop-airdrop-vesting-unspecified), and the teaser adds various prizes (flop-agent-airdrop-basis). Claiming the faucet or holding tokens creates nothing.

rules.statement: Minimum activity - each role has a floor below which no allocation is earned, so dormant accounts do not dilute those that did the work.
rules.consequence: The floor's value is published with the testnet rules, not yet. No screen may imply that any amount of activity is enough.

rules.statement: One participant, one score - wallets under common control are scored as a single participant; dividing activity across accounts earns no additional allocation.
rules.consequence: This tool never suggests splitting activity across keys or wallets. Several keys under one operator are one participant.

rules.statement: Independent demand only - spend routed to a miner under common control, or circulated between wallets under common control, is not credited as demand.
rules.consequence: Paying a miner the user controls, or moving value between the user's own wallets, earns nothing. The executor must never be configured to do either.

rules.statement: Fraud forfeits - an account flagged for manufactured activity forfeits its allocation, subject to appeal within the review window.
rules.consequence: Manufactured activity loses the whole allocation, not just the manufactured part. Combined with the two rules above, wash-like activity is a risk, never a strategy.

rules.statement: Security disclosure - vulnerabilities reported responsibly during the testnet, privately to security@flop.finance, could be eligible for a reward from the ecosystem reserve; exploiting a vulnerability forfeits eligibility.
rules.consequence: The fourth of the testnet page's fairness rules. Exploiting a vulnerability forfeits eligibility. Since the eighth snapshot the page differs in two ways: it adds a condition, that the report is sent privately to security@flop.finance (it named no channel before), and where it said responsible reports are rewarded from the ecosystem reserve it now says such a report could be eligible for a reward from it - from the reserve, not from the airdrop. The airdrop page adds that this is not a bug bounty programme. Nothing in this tool tests the network for weaknesses, and no screen presents exploiting one, or reporting one, as a way to earn.

rules.statement: The record is frozen at a published, finalized block height. Activity after that height is not credited, and no rolling snapshot is taken.
rules.consequence: Only activity up to and including the published snapshot height counts (the Yellow Paper's R8.5: no later than that height). The allocation list and its hash are published before genesis for review and dispute.

rules.statement: Spendable only on inference. Every 3 $FLOP of the locked balance spent in settled sessions unlocks 1 $FLOP, so three quarters is spent on compute and one quarter becomes liquid. There is no end date; balance never spent stays locked.
rules.consequence: The airdrop page (2026-10-05) and the Yellow Paper's normative Agent grant rule both say a locked agent balance unlocks one FLOP for every three of it spent in settled sessions, with no end date; the revenue page and the whitepaper's glossary give the same figure. The teaser and the agent intro page still say the schedule is not set (flop-teaser-agent-release-unset, flop-agent-unlock-ratio-intro); the airdrop page says it follows the Yellow Paper, which is the definitive specification, so this rule carries the formula. Still a draft.

formula.note: Held as data because it is a figure in a draft. Restored from the airdrop page and the Yellow Paper's Agent grant rule (flop-agent-unlock-yellowpaper) on 2026-10-07 after the teaser withdrew it on 2026-09-30 (D-122, D-123). Code reads it from here and never embeds 3. The floor is taken in whatever unit the spend is given in, a simplification of this tool: the Yellow Paper takes floor(K/3) in base units of 10^-18 FLOP (section 1, R8.7), so 5 whole FLOP unlock 1 here and about 1.666666666666666666 FLOP there. Its spend cap - locked compute spend may not exceed floor(3P/4) of the principal P (R8.7) - is not modelled.

rules.statement: Locked agent airdrop can be spent only on compute: opening or topping up inference sessions. When it becomes liquid is not yet set; the Yellow Paper keeps the agent release schedule open.
rules.consequence: The agent intro page still says the release is not set and defers to the Yellow Paper, which now gives the 3:1 rule (flop-agent-unlock-yellowpaper). Its wording has not changed since 2026-09-30; only its navigation and its footer date (2026-10-05) moved. Kept as a quotation so the lag between official pages is visible.

rules.statement: It arrives locked, and a locked balance can be spent only on compute; the schedule on which it becomes liquid is not yet set.
rules.consequence: The teaser still says this, while the airdrop page and the Yellow Paper give a 3:1 spend-to-unlock rule (flop-agent-unlock-ratio). Recorded so the disagreement between official pages is visible rather than resolved silently; screens follow the airdrop page and the Yellow Paper.

rules.statement: It MUST unlock only against spend credit: one FLOP of principal for each three FLOP of its locked part (R8.8) in the payable (Appendix F.3, the gross settlement amount before the audit earmark) of a session settled by settle , by certificate_settle , or by force_settle -> finalize .
rules.consequence: The normative form of the 3:1 rule: only the payable of a settled session counts, and only once its settlement block is finalized, its dispute window has passed and every fraud dispute raised against the session in that window has resolved with none upheld. Spend through agent_transfer, refunds and penalties does not count. Whether a fraud verdict upheld after the window reverses the credit is still open (E.38, following E.44), and the Yellow Paper's status matrix marks R8.7 and R8.8 PARTIAL: the runtime has no Agent spend credit or spend cap yet.

rules.statement: An Agent grant MUST NOT unlock any principal at its start block, and it has no end block.
rules.consequence: Nothing of an agent's airdrop is liquid at genesis, and there is no date by which it must be spent; under R8.7 principal neither spent nor unlocked stays frozen. What finally becomes of Miner and Agent principal that never unlocks is still open in E.38, which also records a residual risk: an agent can pay a miner it controls from locked principal, get about 99% back as that miner's payout and unlock a further third of the spend, and no runtime common-control rule prevents it (E.49).

rules.statement: At the end of the testnet, results are settled into the genesis block. The bulk of the pool is expected to be distributed at the token generation event, with any remainder released at a later stage.
The conversion score, validator activity basis, Validator release order, and reserve disposition remain open in E.38.
rules.consequence: The one-sentence summary of what is still open, at the end of the Yellow Paper's section 8.2. The agent release horizon is no longer on it: an Agent grant unlocks against spend credit with no end block (flop-agent-grant-no-end-block). E.38 itself lists more than the summary, including the disposition of Miner and Agent principal that never unlocks, whether a fraud verdict upheld after the dispute window reverses unlock or spend credit (E.44), publication of operator-held filter inputs and the genesis_reserve release controller. The conversion score that turns testnet spend into an allocation is still open.

rules.statement: The Flop Network account-based system allows agents to do the following: Token transfers Multisig Proxy / authority delegation Validator staking & authority set Miner staking Timelock / vesting Multi-party pool / collaborative escrow Declarative spend-condition layer Have pre-set spend limits
pallet_session_keys + pallet_agent_wallet let an owner pre-authorize a delegate agent with a lifetime cap, per-tx and daily caps, a pallet/destination allowlist, and a circuit breaker
rules.consequence: FLOP's own bounded delegation. LineageAuth's grants are provenance over it, never a replacement for it; when the testnet publishes these pallets, the spend policy in flop/testnet/spend.py must defer to the on-chain caps.

rules.statement: The session-key lifetime MUST be <= 864,000 blocks ( SessionKeysMaxDuration ).
rules.consequence: About ten days at the 1 s target cadence; missed blocks extend it. A prepared action must not assume a session key outlives this.

rules.statement: The owner MUST be able to revoke at any time. Spending MUST be blocked at the session cap (§11 INV-02), the daily cap, and the circuit breaker; a captured session key MUST be bounded by these caps.

The wider composition target is three declarative, bounded, conservation-safe layers: composable spend conditions (Miniscript-style - delivered), attenuable capabilities (UCAN/macaroon-style, generalizing §6.2 session keys - future), and a terminating multi-party escrow (Marlowe-style - the primitive above).
rules.consequence: Attenuable capabilities are named as future work on the base layer. LineageAuth is an off-chain attenuation model today; if FLOP ships one, this tool must map to it rather than compete with it.

rules.statement: The runtime signature type is MultiSignature (signer MultiSigner ), admitting sr25519 , ed25519 , and ecdsa/secp256k1 .
rules.consequence: A FLOP account is not a did:key. An Ed25519 key can sign a FLOP transaction, but the account is an SS58-encoded 32-byte AccountId, and the default scheme is sr25519. No key is held here either way.

rules.statement: Block time One second on average Block reward 96 $FLOP Block halving Every 730 days for the first five halvings
The miner who completes the task successfully earns 85% of the $FLOP inference fee.
rules.consequence: Not the parameters of record: the teaser's banner says settlement pays the miner 99%, with 1% to the audit pool, until the validator fee leg lands (flop-teaser-unratified-figures).

rules.statement: Draft - the normative specification of the protocol. Sections marked planned are not yet implemented.
rules.consequence: The definitive specification the teaser named is now published, as a draft. Every rule taken from it stays official-draft until the Yellow Paper stops calling itself one.

rules.statement:
DELEGATION: a key can say another key acts for it, so an agent holds its own key
instead of being handed yours and you revoke one without moving the other.
rules.consequence: Technocore now carries its own delegation records in DID notes, verified by readers and revoked only by expiry. LineageAuth's Technocore adapter reads rooms and notes; whether it should also read these records is a design question, not something this registry decides.

rules.statement: CAPACITY: at most 300000 rooms, 16777216 notes in total and 300000 per
rules.consequence: Changed at every snapshot so far (163840, 250000, 300000 rooms; 5242880 then 16777216 notes in total) while the per-room history shrank (32 KiB, 20.9 KiB, 17.4 KiB): these are operator settings, read from /config, not protocol. The census percentages in this tool's data are relative to the capacity at the time of each census, not to this figure.

rules.statement: Technocore is a coordination layer, not a settlement system: parties meet and agree in a room, and value moves on some other rail.
rules.derivationNote: The directive's sentence appears verbatim nowhere in flop.finance or the Yellow Paper (which does not mention Technocore). The nearest official text is now the whitepaper (flop-finance-whitepaper, a draft for review, fetched and hashed since the seventh snapshot): section 11 says 'Technocore records what was agreed, by whom and when; it settles nothing and holds no keys.', and section 10 that Technocore 'operates alongside the protocol rather than within it'. The SPEC.md of flop-labs/tclk, from which this entry was first read, was not fetched - only the organisation's repository listing was. The statement therefore stays a derivation, not a quotation, and carries no body hash.

rules.statement: UNKNOWN_FROM_OFFICIAL_SPEC
rules.consequence: No endpoint may be registered as executable.

rules.statement: UNKNOWN_FROM_OFFICIAL_SPEC
rules.consequence: Faucet claims exist only as simulation. The Yellow Paper mentions a faucet only in R8.4, where a faucet grant by itself creates no allocation right (flop-agent-scoring-settled-spend); no source gives the claim procedure, amount or cooldown.

rules.statement: UNKNOWN_FROM_OFFICIAL_SPEC
rules.consequence: Inference spend is never estimated; it is observed or absent. Five session-request fields are named; no wire schema is published.

rules.statement: UNKNOWN_FROM_OFFICIAL_SPEC
rules.consequence: Quotes are simulated and labelled SIMULATION - NO FLOP NETWORK ACTION.

rules.statement: UNKNOWN_FROM_OFFICIAL_SPEC
rules.consequence: Simulation uses an RFC 6761 .invalid origin that cannot resolve. The Yellow Paper sets SS58Prefix = 42 on every FLOP network, so the address prefix does not identify a network; networks are told apart by genesis hash or chain id (R6.5a), and neither value is published.

rules.statement: UNKNOWN_FROM_OFFICIAL_SPEC
rules.consequence: How an agent authenticates to a testnet endpoint is unpublished; chain-transaction signing (sr25519 by default) is a different question and is recorded in flop-account-signature-schemes. No signer is implemented; this tool holds no key and takes no custody.

rules.statement: claim_vested MUST use the finalized head to calculate the unlocked amount, subtract the amount already claimed, and release only a positive remainder from the grant freeze.
rules.consequence: The claim mechanism is specified (R8.8). It runs on mainnet against an allocation written into the genesis block; nothing here can claim, and no screen may present a claim as available before mainnet.
